B2020-099.evidence_locator: Sheet1!A111:O111; Whitlock/Barnosky archive, Neotoma dataset 550, site 534, 1978 central core A, chronology 296, control 1791. Depth 724 cm, thickness 6 cm.
B2020-099.identity: The original investigator archive explicitly uses Mazama as a chronological control. No local glass assay is supplied by the archive.
B2020-099.local_age: Imported 6850 radiocarbon yr BP for the tephra control, limits 6700–7000 on that scale.
B2020-099.age_basis: Core B, a few metres from pollen core A, supplied radiocarbon dates. The 6850 value is an assigned tephra age.
B2020-099.coordinate_basis: S1 lake proxy. The core register calls the station the lake centre, gives site-level 46.59167, -122.25, and supplies no position for the individual core. The published proxies differ by about 5 km.
B2020-099.identity_quality: Source investigator archive and S1 independently describe the same named tephra horizon.
B2020-099.thickness_quality: The explicit 6 cm preserved bed at 724 cm matches both compiled contacts. Core-specific fall, focusing and compaction remain unresolved.

B2020-021.evidence_locator: Sheet1 row 33; Young Table 1.1 row 6 and Fig. 1.14; Mehringer investigator archive 15894 and Columbia River Basin Ecosystems, Steens Mountain profiles, site 37.
B2020-021.coordinate_basis: The compiled position lies inside Mehringer’s Wildhorse Lake site polygon. No individual core GPS fix is archived.
B2020-021.thickness_quality: The investigator record contains 82 pollen samples and no measured contacts for the original in-place fraction. Young’s compilation and the original field studies have different evidential status.

B2020-103.evidence_locator: Sheet1!A115:O115; Mehringer investigator archive 15893, August 1972 collection; Mehringer, Columbia River Basin Ecosystems, Wildcat discussion and site 53; Johnson et al. 1994, Wildcat text and later long core.
B2020-103.identity: Mehringer names the Mazama sequence in this lake and distinguishes later coring. The P/S partition and the numerical primary minimum have not been checked in the original Blinman profile.
B2020-103.coordinate_basis: The compiled point lies inside the investigator’s published Wildcat site polygon. No individual core GPS fixes are archived.
B2020-103.thickness_quality: The 1972 investigator archive has 133 pollen samples and no event thickness or sedimentary contact for the primary component. A later 27.39 m core in 5 m of water is a separate campaign.

B2020-291.evidence_locator: Sheet1 row 303; Young Table 1.1 row 15 and Fig. 1.14; Lichti-Federovich investigator dataset 1656 and associated geochronology 8345. North-bay register, controls 4288/4295; separate 1979 core G1984-LOFTY79.
B2020-291.identity: The north-bay chronology explicitly assigns a Mazama marker. The later 1979 bed is unnamed and is tracked separately.
B2020-291.local_age: Imported horizon ages 6730 radiocarbon yr BP and 7627 cal yr BP in alternative age models of the same north-bay sequence.
B2020-291.age_basis: Chronologies 742 and 743 reuse the tephra rather than supplying independent local dates.
B2020-291.coordinate_basis: Young and S1 site proxy 54.73333, -112.48333. The north-bay data give 54.72528, -112.48083 as site coordinates and no core GPS.
B2020-291.thickness_quality: Chronology controls carry 0.1 cm at 398 cm, but both chronology notes say 598 cm. The 0.2 cm Young bulk-equivalent ceiling has a different evidential basis. The 1979 core separately preserves 0.05 cm at 135 cm without an event identification.
